reason: Partly refuted. The header says every item is 'covered by an existing closure, with no post-hoc relaxation'. That is false for one item, and that item's evidence is invalid. The other items hold. SOUND: (1) ILP_DIVISION_WEIGHT arms other than 0.4. The exp85b dummy moved +49 nodes and +3 forks with LOWREFINE unchanged (CONTEXT 06:26Z), and R23-RC-B found that the relink replaces all ILP edges, so a second ILP arm would have nothing to read. (2) exp85b and exp85c are near-duplicates (the 06:26Z decomposition). (3) cap 10/16, fc2 on cap 8 and thr/DC/tau/N1 are closed by W4 AMEND 2 (4) and S2 (01:02Z). (4) READMIT_RADIUS and the gapfill knobs are undisclosed: 743929 still shows Justin's 04:13Z question unanswered, and feed_loop.log at 07:05:10Z has 0 new comments. FLAWED: READMIT 0.90 or lower. (a) The 'stop rule in R24S-3' was written in this same scan (scan_hyp_slots.json R24S-3: 'never 0.90'), so it is not an existing closure. The only earlier line, R23-RC-A ('never a ladder, no 0.92/0.90'), was already overridden when exp86c (0.92) was built at 06:37Z. That leaves no principled line between 0.92 and 0.90. (b) The cited datum ('[0.94,0.965) 6,696 candidates, 0 near GT') is the one rounds 23 RC-A and RC-C declared LAB-BLIND. In-sample, 99.5% of the GT nuclei that have a peak score >= 0.965, so the datum cannot sign the lever in either direction. Using it as negative evidence repeats the lab over-trust the prompt warns about, and JT read +0.001 on the board at 0.94. The band [0.90,0.94) (4,852 candidates, 2 near GT) is lab-blind in the same way. (c) Discussion 743929 is a disclosed x138-family process, so AGGRESSIVE MODE makes it actionable. Its point 2 says 'One direction better means you step further that way next round', and its point 4 says to build 'deeper steps if the curve is still rising'. An unconditional 0.90 ban, even when 0.92 reads strictly above 0.94, contradicts that process. The rest of the list is correct but adds no value beyond logging, and the R8 statement is honest.
fix: Strike 'READMIT 0.90 or lower' from the closed list and replace it with a pre-registered conditional written before 50/exp86c score: 'RA90(b) = BASE + ILP 0.4 + READMIT_MIN_SCORE 0.90 is allowed ONLY if 50 (exp85a) codes + AND the W2b exp86c (0.92) displays STRICTLY above exp85a. Build it during the exp86c re-run (one --set, CPU only). Push its dummy only on that branch. Gate: validate ok, 0 errors, nodes above RA92(b) (the lab estimate is +0.43% for the [0.90,0.94) band; flag |dn| > 1.5% vs BASE), LOWREFINE refined above RA92(b), forks within +-5. W4 00:45Z takes the slot RA92(b) no longer needs because it is already scored. There is no step below 0.90 and no RA90+CI. Public-only; it enters the finals card only as a public read (winner's curse on the node-addition family, whose sign flips by embryo per R12-NF).' Also correct the evidence text: the 6,696/0 figure is 'lab-blind (R23-RC-A/RC-C)', not a negative read. Also change the header to 'covered by an existing closure or by measured inertness'. Keep every other item.
realistic_gain: Tiny. The 0.90 branch fires with P ~0.3 (50 codes +) x ~0.3 (0.92 strictly above 0.94) ~0.09, and then shows +0.001 public with P ~0.2-0.3, so ~0.02 overall. The private sign is unknown (a node-addition lever, embryo-dependent). The cost is one conditional CPU build plus a ~25 min GPU dummy, and a W4 slot that would otherwise hold E10 or stay empty; runtime is the same as K2 (readmit arms ran 1,388 s vs 1,409 s). The main value is keeping the plan consistent with the disclosed 743929 process and with the R23 lab-blind finding. No score claim follows from it.
